report.summary: Chunk 3 of 3: arm, stop, clear methods, _WatchScope, and CLI _main function. Claims verified against present code.
risks: _main | medium | The CLI parsing for 'arm' passes all remaining words as note, including '--force' if it appears after other args; note may contain '--force'. | Verify that intended behavior is to include '--force' in note or filter it out. Current code filters '--force' from rest only if it is one of the words; if user writes '--force' after a reason, it remains in note.

arm | low | The 'force' parameter deletes marker silently. If marker is a directory, os.unlink may fail and exception is caught. But if marker is a directory and force is True, the marker remains; arm proceeds. | Check if marker could be a directory; consider using os.remove or shutil.rmtree.

handoff.purpose: Defines arm, stop, clear methods, _WatchScope context manager, and CLI entry point _main.

symbols.name: KillSwitch.arm
symbols.note: Writes permit file if no stop marker present (or force=True). Raises LoopHalted if marker present and not force.

symbols.name: KillSwitch.stop
symbols.note: Writes marker first, then permit, both with STOP token. Raises LoopHalted if after writes the switch still reads as running.

symbols.name: KillSwitch.clear
symbols.note: Deletes both marker and permit files; leaves switch stopped.

symbols.name: _WatchScope
symbols.note: Context manager that calls start_watch/stop_watch on a KillSwitch.

symbols.name: _WatchScope.__enter__
symbols.note: Calls start_watch on switch and returns it.

symbols.name: _main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses args and calls appropriate KillSwitch method. Returns exit code.

claims.text: REFUSES if a stop marker is present unless ``force=True``. That refusal is the guard against the most likely way an unattended system undoes a human decision: the loop crashes, a supervisor restarts it, its startup path calls ``arm()``, and the 3am stop evaporates. Re-arming after a deliberate stop has to be a deliberate act.
claims.why: Code in arm checks _marker_present() and raises LoopHalted if present and not force. The reasoning about loop crash/restart is not checkable in code but the behavior matches.

claims.text: MARKER FIRST, and that order is load-bearing twice over: * If the process dies between the two writes, the permit still says ``RUN`` -- but the marker alone already means stop, so the crash window resolves to STOPPED rather than to running. * :meth:`_marker_present` uses ``os.stat``, which does not open the file, so nothing a poller does can block the marker being written. The permit rewrite is the one that can lose a sharing race, and by then the stop has ALREADY taken effect.
claims.why: Code writes marker first (self._marker) then permit (self._path). The claim about os.stat is uncheckable because _marker_present is defined elsewhere, but the order is confirmed.

claims.text: Neither write failing is swallowed and neither is allowed to abort a stop that did take: this raises only if, after both attempts, the switch still reads as running. An operator's stop command must be loud when it did nothing and quiet when it worked.
claims.why: Errors from writes are collected but not raised immediately. After both writes, if read_state().running is True, raises LoopHalted. If running is False, returns state without raising.

claims.text: Remove permit and marker. Leaves the switch STOPPED (no permit).
claims.why: Code deletes both _marker and _path files. After deletion, no permit exists, so switch is stopped.

observations.what: arm method: when force=True, it attempts to unlink the marker and ignores OSError. If unlink fails (e.g., permission), marker may remain and arm proceeds.

stop method: errors from writes are collected but never raised. If both writes fail and read_state still reads as running, the error messages are included in the raised LoopHalted. But if read_state returns not running, errors are silently ignored.

_main function: for 'arm' verb, it filters '--force' from rest only if it is an exact word; if user writes '--force' as part of a longer string, it remains. Also, if '--force' appears after a reason word, it is not removed from note.
